American school kids give the traditional Bellamy salute to the flag during the Pledge of Allegiance. NY. 1915

Francis Bellamy (1855 – 1931) was a Christian socialist minister best known for writing the American Pledge of Allegiance in 1892.

The Bellamy Salute, sometimes known as the Flag Salute, was performed facing the flag during the recital by raising the right arm and pointing the fingers outward. During the 1920s and '30s, Italian fascists and Nazis adopted a salute which had a similar form. This resulted in controversy over the use of the Bellamy salute in the United States. It was officially replaced by the hand-over-heart salute when Congress amended the Flag Code on December 22, 1942.
